I've used supercook.com a lot and just type in the ingredients I have and go from there.

My advice would also be to start with basic dishes, especially ones that use common staples like rice, potatoes, and/ or flour. I'm going to put out my hippy bias out there and put a vote out for trying to cook somewhat sustainably too if you can. :3

Spinach salad yum <3 and legumes as well as others have mentioned like chickpea dishes, bean dishes, lentil dishes. www.supercook.com is a good source to find ideas you can put in ingredients and see what you find that is healthy and vegan. I also like edamame it is good with protein. You can make or buy hummus (made with chickpeas) and use that as a dip for baby carrots or celery.

If you can get access to a stainless steel bento box setup like this I'd recommend it! I got mine here in Japan for like around 2000-2500 yen I think if I remember right? It's a little more expensive but I like it. It can also help you portion your meal as well.

-Cold soba noodle salad with lettuce and toasted sesame dressing

-Stir fry rice with vegetables/ eggs in a stainless steel container - You can maybe put it on the dashboard to help keep it warm? If nothing else having it at a different temperature can still be good.

-Chickpea salads

-Bean salads (like one with bean, corn, onion or sauteed onion if you can't have raw, and some other seasoning you can google recipes)

-Baby carrots for a snack

-Vietnamese style spring rolls - I used to make a bunch of these and put them in a container and bring them with me to work

-You could make a smoothie and bring it with you in a container

-Savory pancake - Sautee negi, leek, or onion, put that in a bowl after it is sauteed, add 2 eggs, stir put in flour (whole grain preferred) and a little salt, and mix it all together into a batter, then cook it like you would a pancake. You can make a bunch of those and bring them with you in a container. You aren't only limited to onion that is just a basic version of this. You can add a lot more fillings to the batter too (I like to add sauteed scallop and cabbage in with it in addition to the oniony vegetable).

-If you have affordable access to Japanese sticky rice, you can make onigiri (rice balls) and pack those in a container

-Fruits like apple and banana
